question.leadin: Answer the following about World War I.
question.text: Led by Franz Joseph the First, this dual-monarchy declared war on Serbia in July 1914.
question.answerHtml: Austria-Hungary (accept Austro-Hungarian Empire/Monarchy; do not prompt on partial answer)
question.clue: This empire formed after the Ausgleich, which made Franz Joseph I its first emperor.

swap.leadin: A bomb thrown at this leader's convertible bounced off and detonated under a nearby car.
swap.text: Name this Austrian archduke and heir to the throne of Austria-Hungary, whose assassination was one of the pivotal causes of World War I.
swap.answerHtml: Archduke Franz Ferdinand (or Franz Ferdinand Carl Ludwig Joseph Maria of Austria)
swap.clue: His wife was never permitted in the royal carriage, as a condition of his marriage to the lower-class woman after he became heir apparent following the death of his cousin Rudolf and father Charles Louis.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the aftermath of the Napoleonic Wars.
question.text: Klemens von Metternich chaired a "Congress" in this Austrian capital that redrew borders and repaired alliances in the aftermath of Napoleon's conquests.
question.clue: Following one battle, cannons captured from the defeated Ottomans were melted down into a bell for this city's St. Stephen's Cathedral.

swap.leadin: This monarch hired the physician Gerard van Swieten to initiate sanitary reforms.
swap.text: Name this Habsburg empress, the mother of Marie Antoinette, who allied with France in the Diplomatic Revolution.
swap.clue: Van Swieten's son served as this ruler's ambassador to Prussia and patronized Mozart.

question.text: According to the Codex Mendoza, the ball game was also played by the Aztecs. The Codex Mendoza was written to help Charles V, a member of this royal family that ruled Austria, to understand Aztec history.
question.clue: Members of this family often used the acronym A.E.I.O.U., including Frederick III.

swap.text: A conference organized by this Austrian Chancellor swiftly formed the Seventh Coalition to fight Napoleon during the Hundred Days. This man represented Francis II at the Congress of Vienna.
swap.answerHtml: Klemens von Metternich [or Klemens Wenzel Nepomuk Lothar, Prince of Metternich-Winneburg zu Beilstein]
swap.clue: The Academic Legion forced this man's resignation during the Revolutions of 1848.

question.text: The death of Rudolf led to political instability in Austria-Hungary culminating in the assassination of this Archduke by Gavrilo Princip.
question.clue: This Austrian Archduke who was assassinated by Gavrilo Princip in 1914, kicking off a series of events leading to the start of World War I.

swap.leadin: Because of his short stature, some of this man's less endearing nicknames included "Millimetternich" and "the Jockey."
swap.text: Name this Chancellor of Austria who proclaimed himself dictator in the May Constitution. He banned the Nazi Party, but a bunch of them managed to assassinate him in the July Putsch of 1934.
swap.clue: This dictator absorbed the Heimwehr of Prince Starhemberg to establish the Fatherland Front, but was assassinated by Otto Planetta during the July Putsch.

question.text: The over-the-top Soviet war memorial in Schwarzenbergplatz in this country's capital city has been targeted by vandals, but it is protected by the 1955 treaty by which Soviet troops ended their occupation of part this country.
question.clue: This country's far-right Freedom Party was led by Jorg Haider (yerg "HI"-der).

swap.text: This 1711 declaration said that the daughters of Holy Roman Emperor Charles VI had precedence in succession over the heirs of former emperors Leopold I and Joseph I.
swap.clue: In 1830, Ferdinand VII of Spain relied on one to insure that he would be succeeded by his daughter.

question.leadin: Answer the following about lesser-known "Wars of Succession" from European history.
question.text: The War of Bavarian Succession saw this Habsburg co-regent of his mother, Maria Theresa, lead his men in the field in Bavaria against Frederick the Great's men, with the Peace of Teschen seeing a small territorial gain for Austria.
question.clue: This ruler sent generals Lacy and Laudon on a series of tactical maneuvers in one conflict that saw little actual fighting, the War of Bavarian Succession, and, in response to the peasants' revolt of Horea, abolished serfdom.

swap.leadin: A rigged referendum used to bring about this event featured a ballot with a large, centered "yes" circle and a smaller "no" circle to the right.
swap.text: Name this 1938 event in which Nazi Germany annexed its southern neighbor. Kurt Schuschnigg ("SHOOSH-nig") was forced to resign for opposing this event.
swap.answerHtml: Anschluss (“ON-sh’loose”) [prompt on, but DO NOT REVEAL, descriptions like German annexation of Austria]
swap.clue: Kurt von Schuschnigg was replaced by Arthur Seyss-Inquart the day before this event, which gathered 99.7% approval in a plebiscite a month after it happened.

question.text: This man believed that the only way to stop the recurring pattern of Jewish migration and persecution was for them to found their own state, which he wrote in his book The Jewish State. He is regarded as the father of Zionism.
question.clue: He could not overcome the opposition of the Russian faction of his confederates to the Uganda plan, nor could he talk the Ottoman Sultan into giving him what he wanted.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the political impact of the death of Rudolf, Crown Prince of Austria, in the Mayerling Incident.
swap.text: As part of a murder-suicide pact, Rudolf killed this teenage lover of his in the Mayerling Incident.

question.text: The Nazi-Austria fun house continued with the affair named for this politician, who served as UN Secretary General from 1972 to 1981. He was discovered to have lied about his Nazi past during his 1986 election campaign.
question.clue: His service in the Kozara mountains involved a massacre of Yugoslavs, and he was also a senior lieutenant during the deportation of forty thousand Jews from Salonika.

swap.text: This person refused to confirm Karl Lueger, founder of the Christian Social Party, as mayor of Vienna until Leo XIII intervened. This man's only son committed suicide with his lover in the Mayerling Incident.
swap.clue: The Fundamental Articles of his minister of commerce and agriculture Albert Schaffle was denounced by German nationalists, and he appeared beside Alexander II in Berlin in 1873 in support of the Dreikaiserbund.

question.leadin: This man's election was vetoed three times by Franz Joseph, who despised him.
question.text: Name this mayor of Vienna from 1897 - 1910, whose virulent anti-semitism may have inspired a young Adolf Hitler.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the short-lived Duchy of Warsaw.
swap.text: This 1809 treaty assigned Krakow and Lublin to the Duchy, and compelled Austria to pay a large indemnity to France and break off trade relations with England.

question.leadin: This leader came to power after his predecessor resigned in protest of the Ninth-of-May Constitution.
question.text: Name this leader who became the first communist President of Czechoslovakia in 1948 after deposing Edvard Benes during Victorious February.

swap.leadin: Both Pope Paul II and the architect Giacomo della Porta allegedly died due to this action.
swap.text: Name this action, which allegedly caused Giacomo della Porta's organs to chill. Holy Roman Emperor Frederick III and his son Maximilian II were both alleged to have died due to this behavior.
swap.answerHtml: eating melons [accept watermelon or cantaloupe in place of melons, prompt on eating or eating fruit with “what specific food?”]
